title: Prefatio §II: The 1703 threefold Pacific Writing, Lutheran approvals, and the Hexads' hostile reception
pass_a_gloss: More willingly I prescribed acquiescence because, stirred by that man, I meditated other Pacific Writings from which Lutheran theologians could judge Protestant controversies had been at least unduly multiplied by quarrelsome doctors, since on Faith's Foundation both parties entirely agree — of which I was already convinced — and my reply to Scultetus would have aimed solely at proving that. Exactly to that counsel, in 1703 came twofold Pacific Writing: one Dogmatically exposing Lutheran-Reformed Consensus in Faith Foundations; other Paradigmatically via Sandomierz Consensus recommending Protestant Union; then Third on Nature of Union to be kept with gentle Response to a Lutheran doctor's judgment on my first tract. Although all Three Writings were approved by excellent Lutheran doctors and Leipzig reviewers March 1705 (Calvor Consultatione p.439; Fabricius Consideratione), yet others — especially after my Hexads merely setting out Dissensus Beyond-Fundamentals — though never injured by me, rushed with anger and envy upon me and all my writings without measure.
pass_b_english: And the more willingly did I prescribe this quiet acquiescence to myself, because, stirred by this same man, I was meditating other Pacific Writings, from which it would be easy for him and for other theologians of the Lutheran party to judge that the Protestant controversies had hitherto been at least unduly multiplied and exaggerated (not to say anything heavier) by certain doctors of a quarrelsome temper especially, since on the Foundation of the Faith both parties entirely agree — of which I was already then most fully convinced in conscience, and afterward more and more fully confirmed; and my whole reply to be rendered to the most distinguished Scultetus would have aimed solely at proving that very point.

Exactly according to the counsel just set out, there came forth in the year 1703 a twofold Pacific Writing: one of them, exposing Dogmatically the Consensus of Lutherans and Reformed in the Foundations of the Faith; the other, Paradigmatically, through the example of the Consensus of Sandomierz, recommending Protestant Union; and a little later a Third supervened, On the Nature and Character of the Union to Be Kept, with an annexed most gentle Response — as was fitting — to the judgment of a certain most upright Lutheran doctor concerning the first of those three little tracts of mine, a doctor who at last in this very year has publicly professed his most celebrated name.

And although all these Three Writings of mine were also approved by the ballot of other most excellent Lutheran doctors besides the most learned Leipzig reviewers of March 1705 (as the most distinguished Cap. Calvor, known even among foreigners, most recently reports in the latest and most praised Consultation he has written On Entering into Ecclesiastical Peace among Protestants, p. 439, himself also voting for the same, both in what immediately precedes and elsewhere, especially pp. 30 and 31 of his Appendix — I pass over in silence for now Johann Fabricius, distinguished alike in theological knowledge and prudence, both in his most clear-sighted Consideration of his Controversies and in his most modest Defense of that Consideration);

yet there have not been wanting others also — especially after those three writings, all pertaining to the Fundamental Consensus of Protestants, had been followed by certain most gentle Hexads of mine, published in Academic fashion and submitted to public inquiry, merely setting out the Protestant Dissensus Beyond-the-Fundamentals — who, though never injured by me with so much as a word, either directly or indirectly through others' sides, were nonetheless so stirred with passion and stung by the gadfly of anger and envy that they rushed upon me and upon all my writings indiscriminately, not once or twice but in almost countless turns and ways, without measure or end, so that they must seem to have abstained from no manner of injury whatever.
source_text:
Tantóque lubentius acquiescendum ita mihi praecepi ipsi, quod alia Scripta Pacifica, per hunc ipsum Virum excitatus, animo meditarer, ex quibus tam illi, quam aliis Lutheranae Partis Theologis, in proclivi futurum esset judicare, Controversias Protestanticas, saltem indebite (ne quid gravius dicam) multiplicatas hactenus ac exaggeratas a quibusdam Theologis cumprimis litigiosae indolis Doctoribus fuisse, cum in Fidei Fundamento Pars utraque (quo de convictissimus in conscientia jam tum eram, magis magisque de eodem posthac pleneque confirmatus) omnino conspiraret; ad quod etiam ipsum unice evincendum, tota mea responsio, Clarissimo Sculteto reddenda, collineatura fuisset.

Ad amussim vero Consilii, modo edisserti, prodibat Anno 1703. duplex Scriptum Pacificum, quorum alterum, Consensum Lutheranorum et Reformatorum in Fidei Fundamentis exponens, Dogmatice, alterum, Paradigmaticé per Sendomiriensis Consensus exemplum, Unionem Protestanticam commendabat, superveniente paulo post Tertio, de Natura ac indole Unionis tuendae, cum annexa placidissima, uti fieri decebat, Responsione ad judicium, de Tractatulo meo trium istorum primo, integerrimi cujusdam Doctoris Lutherani, hoc demum anno nomen suum celeberrimum publice professi.

Etsi vero etiam universa haec Scripta mea Tria, aliorum quoque Doctorum Lutheranorum Excellentissimorum praeter doctissimos Lipsiensium Recensores, de anno 1705. mense Martio, probata fuerint calculo (id quod recentissime refert Vir etiam apud exteros Clarissimus Dn. Cap. Calvorus in novissima quam conscripsit, de Pace Ecclesiastica inter Protestantes ineunda, Consultatione laudatissima, p. 439. ipse met iisdem, tum in proxime antecedentibus, tum alibi, praecipue p. 30. et 31. Appendicis suae, suffragatus; Taceo nunc scientia pariter atque prudentia Theologicis insignem Dn. Joh. Fabricium, tam in Consideratione Controversiarum suarum perspicacissima, quam Defensione Considerationis istius modestissima); tamen non defuerunt quoque alii, praesertim postquam memorata Scripta tria, ad Consensum Protestantium Fundamentalem pertinentia omnia, Dissensum Protestanticum Praeter-Fundamentalem modo exponentes placidissimo Hexades aliquot, more Academico a me divulgatae publicaeque Disquisitioni submissae, excepissent, qui, nullo licet verbo, sive directe, sive per latus aliorum, indirecte, a me unquam laesi, tanta nihilominus animi commotione, tantoque iracundiae livorisque oestro perciti, in me, Scriptaque mea promiscue omnia, non semel atque iterum, sed innumeris pene vicibus modisque, sine modo vel termino, ita irruerunt, ut a nullis omnino injuriandi modis se abstinuisse videri debeant.
